audit.whatIsWrong: Level-chart stages carried a closing verdict that contradicted the stage owner (for example a stage marked Gnar ending "Camille is favoured here").
audit.why: The full-layer phase text was templated; the tail sentence was never reconciled with phases[].side, so the written verdict and the chart disagreed on the same page.
audit.corrected: Each phase why now closes with the verdict that matches its own side field, so early / mid / side-lane ownership reads consistently.

audit.why: Spike stages line up with the real kits: Camille at 2 (Hookshot, 16s at rank 1), 6 (The Hextech Ultimatum, 140s at rank 1) and her Sheen item; Gnar at GNAR! (90/60/30).

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 stage told you to "use the cast's brief untargetable frame" on The Hextech Ultimatum to dodge Gnar's key spell.
audit.why: Riot's own description of The Hextech Ultimatum is "Camille dashes to target champion, anchoring them to the area" — there is no untargetable window. The kit file's untargetable/channel flags on R are tooltip-parse misfires and contradict the description.
audit.corrected: The stage now says the dash grants no immunity and keys R to being spent after the enemy spell rather than into it.

edits.before: Short shield-window trades. Start W (Tactical Sweep) for the outer-edge poke and heal, or Q for the empowered auto into a melee threat. Do not extend past your Adaptive Defenses shield or your raw HP falls behind. Gnar is favoured here.
edits.after: Short shield-window trades. Start W (Tactical Sweep) for the outer-edge poke and heal, or Q for the empowered auto into a melee threat. Do not extend past your Adaptive Defenses shield or your raw HP falls behind. Camille is favoured here.

edits.before: Full early kit with W online. Space the outer blade to heal, weave the empowered second Q for true damage, and keep E held until GNAR! is committed. Camille is favoured here.
edits.after: Full early kit with W online. Space the outer blade to heal, weave the empowered second Q for true damage, and keep E held until GNAR! is committed. Gnar is favoured here.

edits.before: Your Q ranks amplify the true-damage second hit, so short chunk trades favour you. Freeze the wave on your side to build run-down corridors when you are ahead. Camille is favoured here.
edits.after: Your Q ranks amplify the true-damage second hit, so short chunk trades favour you. Freeze the wave on your side to build run-down corridors when you are ahead. Gnar is favoured here.

edits.before: The Hextech Ultimatum (R) isolates a target in a 1v1 they cannot leave. Use the cast's brief untargetable frame to dodge Gnar's GNAR! or burst, then focus the trapped target. Gnar is favoured here.
edits.after: The Hextech Ultimatum (R) isolates a target in a 1v1 they cannot leave. The dash grants no immunity, so spend R once Gnar's GNAR! is gone, not into it, then focus the trapped target. Camille is favoured here.

edits.before: Trinity Force / Sheen turns your Q resets lethal and your wall dives become kill threats. Start applying deep side-lane pressure and clearing camps between waves. Camille is favoured here.
edits.after: Trinity Force / Sheen turns your Q resets lethal and your wall dives become kill threats. Start applying deep side-lane pressure and clearing camps between waves. Gnar is favoured here.

edits.before: Elite split-push duelist — your true-damage Q2 cuts straight through armor stacking. Camille is favoured here.
edits.after: Elite split-push duelist — your true-damage Q2 cuts straight through armor stacking. Gnar is favoured here.

edits.before: Level 1 belongs to Gnar — his boomerang (Q) and hop-autos out-range your single point of Precision Protocol, so don't walk up to throw a Q he just side-steps. Take the chip and last-hit. The moment you hit Level 2-3 the lane flips: with the second Q point (the true-damage recast) plus a point in W Tactical Sweep and E, you can E-in, land W's outer edge for the max-HP slow, and connect the second Q hit before he can hop back. Your Adaptive Defense passive shields his first hop-auto as you close, so bait his boomerang toss, then commit — his poke can't out-sustain your W heal.
edits.after: Level 1 belongs to Gnar — his boomerang (Q) and hop-autos out-range your single point of Precision Protocol, so don't walk up to throw a Q he just side-steps. Take the chip and last-hit. The moment you hit Level 2-3 the lane flips: with the second Q point (the true-damage recast) plus a point in W Tactical Sweep and E, you can E-in, land W's outer edge for the max-HP slow, and connect the second Q hit before he can hop back. Your Adaptive Defenses passive shields his first hop-auto as you close, so bait his boomerang toss, then commit — his poke can't out-sustain your W heal.

notes: Camille kit file flags R as channel/interruptible and untargetable; both contradict Riot's own description (a dash plus an anchoring zone) and were treated as tooltip-parse misfires, per the kit README. Packet win rate 52.88% over 399 games.
